---
title: Real spectral theorem 
---

## Statement and proof {-}

$\mc{M}^{n \times n}$ denotes the set of $n \times n$ matrices. $\mc{S}^{n \times n} \subset \mc{M}^{n \times n}$ denotes the set of *symmetric real valued* $n \times n$ matrices.

::: {#thm-real-spectral-theorem}
**[Real spectral theorem]{style="color: red;"}**

Let $\bsf{F} \in \mc{S}^{n \times n}$. Then there exists an orthonormal basis of $\mbb{R}^{n}$ consisting of the eigenvectors of $\bsf{F}$ and a diagonal matrix $\bsf{D}$ such that
$$
    \bsf{F} = \bsf{N} \bsf{D} \bsf{N}^{\msf{T}}
$$
where $\bsf{N} \in \mc{M}^{n \times n}$ whose columns are the *eigenvectors* of $\bsf{F}$ and the elements of the diagonal matrix $\bsf{D}$ are the *eigenvalues* of $\bsf{F}$. Further, the matrices $\bsf{N}$ and $\bsf{D}$ *need not be unique*.
:::

::: {#exm-real-spectral-theorem}
Let $n = 3$. Then $\bsf{D}$ and $\bsf{N}$ can be written as
$$
\bsf{D} =
    \begin{pmatrix}
    \lambda_{1} & 0 & 0 \\
    0 & \lambda_{2} & 0 \\
    0 & 0 & \lambda_{3}
    \end{pmatrix}
\quad
\bsf{N} =
    \begin{pmatrix}
    ^{1}N_{1} & ^{2}N_{1} & ^{3}N_{1} \\ 
    ^{1}N_{2} & ^{2}N_{2} & ^{3}N_{2} \\
    ^{1}N_{3} & ^{2}N_{3} & ^{3}N_{3}
    \end{pmatrix}
$$
where $\lambda_{i}$ is the $i$-th eigenvalue (the eigenvalues need not be ordered) and $^{d}N_{i}$ is the $i$-th component of the $d$-th eigenvector.
:::

::: {#prf-real-spectral-theorem}
**[Proof of the real spectral theorem]{style="color: blue;"}**

To be completed.
:::

The spectral theorem also implies that the symmetric matrix $\bsf{F}$ can be written as
$$
    \bsf{F} = \sum_{i = 1}^{n} \lambda_{i} \, ^{i}\bsf{N} \otimes ^{i}\bsf{N}
$$

So, if $n = 3$ for example, 
$$
    \bsf{F} = \lambda_{1} \, ^{1}\bsf{N} \otimes ^{1}\bsf{N} + \lambda_{2} \, ^{2}\bsf{N} \otimes ^{2}\bsf{N} + \lambda_{3} \, ^{3}\bsf{N} \otimes ^{3}\bsf{N}
$$
